chapter: Church, Creole life and Mobile musicians
title: Cootie Williams and Silas, two Mobile boys he taught
summary: He recalls Cootie Williams, whom he gave lessons and who loved shooting craps, and a boy Silas who later played clarinet in England.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And so, Mobiliar's had a good many musicians. Now we got, we got a couple of boys from Mobiliar. One's over in England somewhere, he was a little fella. He picked up around here and was in the Lipskins band. Well, he practically wasn't exactly in the band, he'd just go along with them and play a little at the time. And one of the fellas was taking interest in him and started teaching him the music well. He was playful and he didn't seem to take to it too much. One of them was playing corinette and one of them was playing corn. Now one was running the corinette. He loves to gamble and he get around to practice. He stopped practicing to go try to gamble. He didn't pay much attention to music. So finally, I don't know, he left Mobiliar. He's taking it up in his head and he's leaving some of the biggest orchestras in Chicago. And he's got his orchestras on. When I last heard from him about eight, ten years ago, he bought his mother a $30,000 home. You see? He's made good up there. What was his name? Cootie Williams. Oh yes, Chris Williams. Cootie Williams. He was with Duke Ellington a long time. Yeah, that's him. And I gave him one or two lessons, you know, what we called the Cowboys band. He didn't pull out on a comical parade, you know. And I gave him one or two lessons with Nolly Daniel. And he was one of them fellas that wasn't paying much attention, but now he got him all. He's famous now. And another boy, his name was Silas, and he disappeared all at once. The next thing we heard from him, he was over in England. And he'd done learning his clarinet and playing in Augustus over in England. What was his name? His first name was Silas, but I never did know him. Silas. Well, maybe we'll find out someday, his full name. But I don't know, he may be living now, but he left, and when we heard from him, he was over in England. And playing, and learned his clarinet. But those two boys, they didn't pay much attention when someone was trying to teach them. Especially Cootie, he loved to shoot crafts. Yeah. We'd be on jobs sometime, and when they'd have intermission, he'd go out there and find Cootie shooting craft. I'll tell you. He'd be intermission. But now he's got him orchestra, and they'd bought him his mother thirty thousand dollars.
Is folks still here, some of them, are they? Huh?
Or some of his folks? Yes, some of his folks are here. Yes, sir.
